source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ABG indicates respiratory acidosis?
questions.rationale: In respiratory acidosis, pH falls and PCO2 rises (opposite directions).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1300 (PDF p. 1601)
questions.quote: In respiratory acidosis, the pH is decreased and an opposite effect is seen in the Pco2

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which PaO2 shows a client's oxygen level is adequate?
questions.rationale: Normal PO2 is 80 to 100 mm Hg.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1304 (PDF p. 1606)
questions.quote: The normal Po2 level is 80 to 100 mm Hg.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where should a client with active TB be placed?
options: A ward with other TB clients
questions.rationale: Active TB requires a private room with good ventilation (6 to 12 air exchanges per hour).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1307 (PDF p. 1609)
questions.quote: a client with TB requires a private room.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why are lipids given to a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: Fat emulsions prevent essential fatty acid deficiency and help meet caloric needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1309 (PDF p. 1611)
questions.quote: administered to clients who are at risk for developing an essential fatty acid deficiency

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before surgery, which medication should the nurse PRIORITIZE asking the surgeon about holding?
questions.rationale: Warfarin is often withheld before surgery to reduce bleeding risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1314 (PDF p. 1616)
questions.quote: This medication is often withheld for a period of time preoperatively

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which observation of home oxygen use needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The concentrator needs clear space for air circulation; enclosed spaces can overheat and cause fire.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1318 (PDF p. 1620)
questions.quote: The oxygen concentrator should be free and clear of walls or other enclosed spaces

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which belongs in the plan for a client scheduled for bronchoscopy?
questions.rationale: Dentures, contact lenses, and prostheses are removed before sedation, and informed consent is signed. The client is NPO.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1324 (PDF p. 1626)
questions.quote: If the client has any contact lenses, dentures, or other prostheses, they are removed before sedation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A healthy client (HIV-negative) has 8 mm induration on a Mantoux test. How is this read?
questions.rationale: For people without immunosuppression, 8 mm is below the positive cutoff (10 mm under PH guidelines). 5 mm or more is positive only for HIV or immunosuppressed clients.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1325 (PDF p. 1627)
questions.quote: More than 5 mm of induration is considered a positive result for clients with known or suspected human immunodeficiency virus

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test must be positive before drawing radial ABGs?
questions.rationale: The Allen test confirms ulnar collateral flow before radial puncture.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1326 (PDF p. 1628)
questions.quote: The Allen test is performed before drawing ABGs.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding in hypercalcemia needs follow-up?
questions.rationale: Hypercalcemia raises the risk of clots; poor capillary refill may signal impaired circulation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1350 (PDF p. 1653)
questions.quote: The client with hypercalcemia is at risk for formation of blood clots.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement about TENS shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I must stay in hospital to use it.'
questions.rationale: TENS is portable and client-controlled; hospitalization is not required.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1352 (PDF p. 1655)
questions.quote: It is not necessary for the client to remain in the hospital for this treatment.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea should be assessed for which sign?
questions.rationale: Dehydration causes weight loss, lethargy, sunken eyes, poor turgor, tachycardia, and hypotension.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1379 (PDF p. 1682)
questions.quote: The client described in the question will most likely be dehydrated

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is on 1200 mL/day fluid restriction. How much is usually allowed on the 7 am–3 pm shift?
questions.rationale: About half the allotment is given on the day shift when the client is most active and takes meals and medicines.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1380 (PDF p. 1683)
questions.quote: the nurse informs the dietary department and discusses the allotment of fluid per shift with the dietitian.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a common adult bone marrow biopsy site?
questions.rationale: The iliac crest and sternum are rich in marrow and easily accessible.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1387 (PDF p. 1690)
questions.quote: The most common sites for bone marrow biopsy in the adult are the iliac crest and the sternum.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which advice promotes PRIMARY prevention of cervical cancer?
questions.rationale: Early treatment of cervical infection prevents chronic cervicitis, which can lead to premalignant dysplasia. Douches are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1389 (PDF p. 1692)
questions.quote: Early treatment of cervical infection can help prevent chronic cervicitis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After EGD and vital signs, what is the nurse's next priority?
questions.rationale: The return of the gag reflex is checked first to protect the airway. Sharp pain may signal perforation and is also monitored.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1398 (PDF p. 1702)
questions.quote: The nurse places highest priority on assessing for the return of the gag reflex

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which pre-test action shows a client understands barium swallow instructions?
questions.rationale: The client removes metal objects and is usually NPO before the radiograph.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1400 (PDF p. 1704)
questions.quote: The client is told to remove metal objects

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with AKI has heavy proteinuria. Which type of kidney failure is likely?
questions.rationale: Intrinsic failure shows fixed specific gravity and proteinuria. Prerenal has high specific gravity and little protein.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1420 (PDF p. 1726)
questions.quote: With intrinsic (intrarenal) renal failure, there is a fixed specific gravity, and the urine tests positive for proteinuria.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which home instruction is correct for an adult with influenza?
questions.rationale: Influenza spreads by droplets; handwashing and staying home prevent spread. Fluids and rest help.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1424 (PDF p. 1733)
questions.quote: It is a communicable disease spread by droplet infection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Right after TURP, a client suddenly becomes confused. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Hypotonic flushing solution absorbed during TURP can cause hyponatremia, an early sign of which is confusion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1430 (PDF p. 1739)
questions.quote: The client who suddenly becomes disoriented and confused after TURP could be experiencing early signs of hyponatremia.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hip prosthesis surgery, which attendant action needs intervention?
options: Seating her on a low commode
questions.rationale: The client must not flex the hip beyond 90 degrees; a low commode does this. The seat should be raised.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1435 (PDF p. 1744)
questions.quote: a client should not flex the body more than 90 degrees relative to the chair

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with CKD understands potassium restriction?
questions.rationale: Boiling and discarding the water reduces potassium. Salt substitutes are high in potassium.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1436 (PDF p. 1745)
questions.quote: The potassium content of vegetables can be reduced by boiling them and discarding the cooking water.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A pale client reports fatigue and dizziness. Which lab result is the priority for planning care?
questions.rationale: Pallor, fatigue, and dizziness fit anemia, so the low hemoglobin guides care.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1440 (PDF p. 1749)
questions.quote: the nurse uses the hemoglobin results to plan care because the client’s clinical indicators are consistent with anemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign suggests anemia after postoperative blood loss?
questions.rationale: Low hemoglobin reduces oxygen-carrying capacity, causing fatigue.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1448 (PDF p. 1757)
questions.quote: The client with anemia is likely to report fatigue caused by deficient hemoglobin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most frequent cause of pain after TURP?
questions.rationale: Bladder spasms from distention or the catheter balloon are common; antispasmodics are given.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1456 (PDF p. 1765)
questions.quote: Bladder spasms can occur after this surgery

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which breakfast item INCREASES lower esophageal sphincter pressure in GERD?
questions.rationale: Nonfat milk increases LES pressure; coffee, chocolate, and fats decrease it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1457 (PDF p. 1766)
questions.quote: The food substance that will increase the LES pressure is nonfat milk.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test detects circulating RBC antibodies when screening blood compatibility?
questions.rationale: The indirect Coombs test detects circulating RBC antibodies and is part of 'type and screen'.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1459 (PDF p. 1768)
questions.quote: The indirect Coombs’ test detects circulating antibodies against red blood cells

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with burns over 25% TBSA has early labs. Which value is expected?
questions.rationale: Fluid shifts out of vessels, causing hemoconcentration and a high hematocrit.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1475 (PDF p. 1784)
questions.quote: Hematocrit levels elevate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a panic attack: pH 7.49, PCO2 31, HCO3 22. Which imbalance?
questions.rationale: pH above 7.45 with PCO2 below 35 and normal HCO3 is respiratory alkalosis from hyperventilation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1480 (PDF p. 1789)
questions.quote: Respiratory alkalosis is present when the Pco2 is less than 35

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Low serum transferrin and low TIBC suggest which cause of anemia?
questions.rationale: Malnutrition lowers transferrin and TIBC. Iron deficiency usually raises TIBC.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1499 (PDF p. 1808)
questions.quote: Malnutrition can cause reductions in the serum transferrin and the TIBC.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which anemia is diagnosed with a Schilling test?
questions.rationale: The Schilling test identifies the cause of vitamin B12 deficiency, which underlies pernicious anemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1500 (PDF p. 1809)
questions.quote: The Schilling test is used to determine the cause of vitamin B12 deficiency

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement about ERCP needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: IV sedation (not oral) is given, with an anesthetic throat spray to prevent gagging.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1503 (PDF p. 1812)
questions.quote: Intravenous sedation (not oral) is given to relax the client

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A young adult with sarcoidosis says there's no point learning self-care since there's no cure. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: Powerlessness is feeling no control over the situation or outcome.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1516 (PDF p. 1826)
questions.quote: The client with powerlessness expresses feelings of having no control over a situation or outcome.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What must be done FIRST before a leg fracture is reduced in the casting room?
questions.rationale: Informed consent for treatment is obtained before reduction, with explanations reinforced.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1534 (PDF p. 1845)
questions.quote: Before a fracture is reduced, an informed consent for treatment is needed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with new AKI has potassium 6.1 mEq/L. What should the nurse do IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia risks dysrhythmias and arrest; the provider is notified at once for treatment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1538 (PDF p. 1849)
questions.quote: The client with hyperkalemia is at risk of developing cardiac dysrhythmias and resultant cardiac arrest.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which item is allowed on a clear liquid diet?
questions.rationale: Clear liquids are transparent and liquid at body temperature: water, tea, broth, and gelatin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1546 (PDF p. 1858)
questions.quote: A clear liquid diet consists of foods that are relatively transparent to light
